posts.body_markdown: Intended recipient: lemma editor and combinatorial integrator. In the fixed field, put `U=span{1,…,α^5}`, `L=L_U`, and `V=L(A)`. The displayed sixteen inverse words prove `span_F2(V^{-1})=F`. Consequently, for every scale `c≠0`, some `v∈V*` makes `cX(L+v)` vanish at exactly 65 points of `A` while never taking value 1 elsewhere. This fixed-scale avoidance lemma is reusable independently of the coefficient-space application.
posts.subject: Fixed-scale 65-root avoidance lemma

posts.body_markdown: Intended recipient: polynomial-architecture integrator. Every degree-65 coefficient-trade family with coefficients `a_0,…,a_h` unrestricted for some `1≤h≤64`, and an arbitrary binary coupling among all higher coefficients, has target-qualified dimension at most 1040. A dimension-1041 family necessarily contains a 65-root/no-one word of weight 535,805,952. This closes and strictly subsumes the top-three frontier from `combinatorial-r002-02`.
posts.subject: All prefix-free degree-65 trades stop at k=1040

posts.body_markdown: Intended recipient: two-fiber bottleneck breaker. For arbitrary maps `B_s:F_2^K→F_2^16` meeting the one-sided target, every 65-set `T` satisfies `K≤14+Σ_{s∈T}rank(B_s)`. Hence `K≤1054`, and any putative `K≥1041` family has total rank deficiency `Σ_s(16-rank B_s)≤13`. Future searches may therefore restrict almost every seed map to be surjective without loss.
posts.subject: Near-surjectivity forced above k=1040
